visual_appeal: Replace the tightly segmented XP bars with continuous fills, a subtle vertical bevel and at most four milestone ticks. The repeated black divisions dominate both the hero and roster, making the interface look like a bank of LED meters rather than a crafted Warcraft panel.
Remove the blurred terminal glow on roster bars, or restrict it to a 2 px highlight inside the fill. Keep state colour concentrated in the fill, chip and 3 px left rail.

Give the outer frame a stronger material hierarchy: a 3 px dark iron perimeter in #17191B, a 1 px bronze inner lip in #806039, and four restrained corner fasteners. The current many thin gold rectangles look assembled rather than art-directed.
play_next_clarity: Move 'Seen 4d ago' out of the gold switching instruction and into the hero's identity metadata. Keep the action on its own line: 'Next: log out and select Le Nette.'

Replace the tiny 'Open card >' text with an approximately 88 × 24 px button, and make the entire hero a clearly highlighted card-opening target. Do not style the switching instruction as an executable character-switch button.

In compact tooltips, replace 'Not resting · in 27d 22h' with 'Not resting · full in ~27d'. The current abbreviated copy is ambiguous beside the main roster's '27d here'; distinguish estimated fill time from time spent at a location.
character_identity: Increase roster portraits from 40 to 44 px and retain the separate class medallion, but limit the medallion to 14 px with a 1 px dark outline so it does not obscure the jaw.

For the live-portrait fallback, avoid showing the same emblem as both the large portrait and its attached class badge, as happens for Jacques Hammer. Use a race silhouette or an initial over a textured shield for the main fallback.

Keep the atmospheric stage and speech treatment, but give the character name a consistent 22 px size and reserve a separate 13 px metadata line below it. Account and last-seen information should never compete with the character's name.
default_theme: Make the oak grain legible primarily on the title rail and outer frame; keep information wells at #100E0C. Currently the default is competent dark-and-gold chrome, but the wood is too understated to establish a distinctive identity.
Replace the bright yellow stock close glyph with a restrained bronze cross on dark red enamel: #79251F face, #B88748 edge, 22 × 22 px visible button and at least 26 × 26 px hit area.
Use one consistent button family for Compact, Link account and Open card: 24 px height, 1 px bronze edge and cream #EAD9B5 labels. The current controls feel borrowed from different interface systems.
elvui_wc3_fit: Fix the title integration before approval: the ElvUI renders show a cramped central title plate with a conspicuous right-hand bracket or seam. Allocate the measured title width plus 32 px padding and remove overlapping title-frame pieces.

Increase the title rail to approximately 30 px and restore a continuous dark iron silhouette around it. The rendered ElvUI version loses the default's material coherence and reads as flat strips surrounding a different interior.

Use the installed skin's supported textures and controls for a consistent red Compact button, bronze framing and corner treatment. If its generic portrait-frame handler cannot provide a coherent result, offer an explicit 'Use Rested Leveling frame with ElvUI fonts' option rather than treating the handler call alone as successful visual integration.

Validate the result in game against the user's actual UI. I am not counting the simulator's lighter washes as a defect, but correcting those washes alone will not supply the missing plank, iron and enamel hierarchy.
alerts_ux: Make 'Hearth first' a separate gold action-emphasis line or a genuine 92 × 24 px action when supported. In the logout render it is buried at the end of the explanatory sentence.
Replace 'Right-click: stop these warnings' with 'Right-click: disable logout warnings'. Keep the explicit close button for dismissing only this alert; permanent suppression should be unambiguous.

In the rested-XP-used-up toast, identify whose XP ran out: 'Jacques Hammer: rested XP used up', followed by 'Play next: Le Nette'. The current portrait belongs to the recommendation while the headline describes another character.
Give the Esc-menu warning strip its own 18 × 18 px dismiss control and an explicit options toggle. Do not rely on the larger logout banner's dismissal affordance to explain this separate surface.
readability: Raise roster names to 15 px and supporting text to 13 px at addon-native scale, with approximately 56–58 px rows. The ElvUI full-screen render is visibly dense, especially the bar captions and state chips.

Remove the redundant calendar deadline from each bar caption. Use '93% · full in 14h 25m' and move the exact day/time to a tooltip; this also prevents long location text from pressing into the bar column.
Use #EADFCB for primary supporting text and no darker than #B8AC98 for secondary text on dark wells. Increase chip text to 12 px and allow 108 px width for 'NOT RESTING'.
Offer a readable-scale preset that maintains at least 12 screen pixels for secondary text after UI scaling, rather than judging legibility only from the enlarged roster crop.
layout_polish: Resolve the visible truncation of long row metadata such as Stonetalon Mountains with a measured text boundary and ellipsis, leaving at least 12 px before the XP column.
Give account tags and Well Rested moons dedicated slots rather than stacking them opportunistically at the row edge. Reserve a 60 px trailing column and align each element consistently.

Rework the history chart into a continuous area or line with a clear full threshold. In the full-rest card, the gold bars sit below the green full line and there is no visible 'Full the whole time' explanation, making a full history look sub-full.
Reduce the character card's repeated framing: use one stage frame, one stats region and one chart frame rather than individually outlining every tile. Keep 8 px gutters and 10–12 px section spacing.
delight: Keep the character-specific speech, warm inn setting and cold outdoor setting; those are the strongest personality elements. Add a restrained 200 ms speech-bubble reveal and a single settling motion when opening a card, respecting reduced-motion preferences.

Replace some repetitive system language with short state-specific character lines while retaining factual labels: for example, 'Ready when you are' for full rest and 'Get me to an inn' for an unrested logout.

Use a small lantern or moon ornament as the distinctive brand motif instead of multiplying generic gold borders. Carry it through the title, empty state and toast without adding continuous glow or animation.

overall_notes: The recommendation hierarchy and four-state colour system work immediately, and the portraits, atmospheric cards and parchment speech give this a stronger identity than a typical utility addon. The main weaknesses are miniature supporting text, excessively segmented bars, repetitive boxed chrome and an ElvUI variant that is less coherent than the default. This is a promising, usable addon, not yet a demanding-user visual sign-off. I have not penalized absent simulator models or live portraits, and I have separated the documented colour-rendering limitation from actual framing and layout problems. The next pass should prioritize readability, title-frame integration and material hierarchy rather than adding more decoration.
